title: Root architecture: from a root picture to a working model
summary: An original, passive-listening explanation of the OpenSimRoot methods paper: how root growth rules, carbon costs, soil resources, and measured root images can be connected, with careful limits and a sorghum modeling interpretation.

scope_note: The primary source is an original methods/model-development paper, not a review or a new field-yield trial. Earlier experiments cited by that paper are explicitly identified as earlier work. Statements about the 2017 software version are time-bounded. Sorghum/CPlantBox/DuMuX applications are interpretation and proposed tests, not findings of the source paper.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement and connections of roots in space and time.
vocabulary.example: Two plants can have the same root length but different root system architecture.

vocabulary.definition: A model that connects the shape of a plant with processes such as growth and uptake.
vocabulary.example: A functional–structural model links root position with water uptake.

vocabulary.definition: A short piece of a root represented between two points.
vocabulary.example: Each root segment can have its own age and diameter.
Gravitropism influences the direction in which a root grows.

vocabulary.definition: The process through which living cells release energy for their activities.
vocabulary.example: Root respiration is part of the carbon cost of soil exploration.

vocabulary.definition: A change in development in response to environmental conditions.
vocabulary.example: Root plasticity can change branching in a nutrient-rich patch.

vocabulary.definition: Greater uptake from one region when another region supplies less.
vocabulary.example: Roots in wet soil may provide compensatory uptake.

vocabulary.definition: Movement of water through roots from wetter soil into drier soil.
vocabulary.example: A root network can sometimes enable hydraulic redistribution.

vocabulary.definition: An area where a resource concentration falls because roots remove it.
vocabulary.example: The simulation estimates a nitrate depletion zone around the roots.

vocabulary.definition: How a plant shares carbon among organs and processes.
vocabulary.example: A carbon-allocation rule can influence the growth of side roots.
